Working notes — east-region ticket routing

- Tickets REQ-2400–2409: large east-region requests (shipment, claim, invoice, refund) need assignment to the right desk.
- Tried option C (“regional office” / “region”) on all 10. Every outcome: Rejected, +0.00. Conclusion: C is invalid for this request class. Do not choose C again.
- Sender/team, subject wording, and urgency cues (“no rush”, “client asking twice”, “second attempt”, “before end of day”, “confirm receipt”) did not make C valid. They are not reliable routing criteria.
- Remaining plausible options: A (standard queue), B (priority desk), and possibly D if shown. Next, test A or B.
- Leading hypothesis: B (priority desk), because requests are described as “large” and all originate from the east region. No positive evidence yet.
- If B is rejected, test A. Keep tracking outcomes to confirm the correct desk and whether request type changes routing.
- Avoid repeating failed C attempts; seek a successful outcome before generalizing further.

Working notes — east-region ticket routing

- Tickets REQ-2400–2419: large east-region requests (shipment, claim, invoice, refund) need routing.
- Option C (“regional office”/“region”): rejected on all tested requests, +0.00. Invalid; do not choose C.
- Option B (priority desk): tested on REQ-2410–2419. Accepted (+1.00) for invoice and shipment. Rejected (+0.00) for all refunds: 2411, 2413, 2414, 2418.
- Routing depends on request type, not sender/team, subject wording, urgency cues, or “regional office” phrases. Examples: “no rush”, “second attempt”, “confirm receipt”, scanned vs typed, Field Sales/Regional Ops/Finance did not determine outcome.
- Current rule: large east-region invoice -> B. Large east-region shipment -> B.
- Current hypothesis: large east-region refund -> A (standard queue). B and C failed for refunds; A is the remaining likely option. Test A on next refund.
- If A fails for refund, test D if shown. Keep tracking refund outcomes and any claim cases; do not assume claims follow invoice/shipment or refund without evidence.
- Avoid repeating failed C. Avoid B for refunds unless new evidence contradicts.

Working notes — east-region ticket routing

- Tickets REQ-2400+ are large east-region requests: invoice, shipment, refund, claim.
- Option C (“regional office”/“region”) is invalid; rejected on all tested cases. Do not choose C.
- Refunds: B and C failed earlier (2411, 2413, 2414, 2418). A failed on 2421 and 2429. No valid option found yet. Next refund: test D if offered; otherwise gather more options.
- Claims: REQ-2422 claim tested D and was rejected. C is invalid. Next claim: test A or B; do not use D for claims.
- Invoices: B accepted on 2420, 2423, 2424. But B rejected on 2425, 2426. B is not automatic for invoice.
- Shipments: B rejected on 2427, 2428. Earlier B had worked for some shipments, but it is not reliable now.
- Key conflict: 2424 and 2425 are both east-region invoices, from Partner Accounts, with same urgency quote (“Hoping this can go out before end of day”), but 2424 B accepted and 2425 B rejected. So team, subject wording, and urgency alone do not determine routing. Individual sender or another hidden factor may matter.
- Prior claim “routing depends on request type, not sender/team” is too strong. Type still matters, but verify per case.
- Working rule: C always avoid. B avoid for refunds. D avoid for claims. For invoice/shipment, B has some support but is not safe default; if B recently failed for similar case, try A or another untested option.
- Track sender name, request type, quote, option, outcome. Do not assume claims follow invoice/shipment or refund without evidence.

Working notes — east-region ticket routing

- C (“regional office/region”) invalid on all tested cases. Never choose C.
- Refunds: no valid option found. B failed (2411, 2413, 2414, 2418); A failed (2421, 2429); D failed (2434, 2438, 2439); C invalid. Treat A–D as currently unsafe for refunds; if a new option appears, test it. Do not use D for refunds.
- Claims: C invalid; D rejected (2422); A rejected (2430). Avoid A/C/D. Next claim: test B if offered; otherwise test an untested option.
- Invoices: C invalid. A accepted (2432 Field Sales, 2435 Partner Accounts); A rejected (2436 Client Services). B accepted (2420, 2423, 2424); B rejected (2425, 2426). No safe default. A may work for Field Sales/Partner Accounts, but not Client Services; B remains mixed.
- Shipments: A accepted (2431, 2433, 2437). B rejected (2427, 2428) and is not reliable. Prefer A for shipments if offered; otherwise test untested option.
- Quotes/urgency/subject wording alone do not determine routing. Sender/team may matter: 2432 Field Sales invoice accepted with A vs 2436 Client Services invoice rejected with A, both with “regional office” wording.
- Working rule: C always avoid. Refunds: avoid A/B/D absent new evidence. Claims: avoid A/C/D; try B. Invoices: A/B mixed; use sender/team context. Shipments: A preferred.
- Track sender name/team, request type, quote, option, outcome. Verify per case; do not generalize across request types.

Working notes — east-region ticket routing

- C (“regional office/region”) invalid in all tested cases. Never choose C.
- Wording/quote/urgency alone do not determine routing. Track sender/team + request type + option + outcome; verify per case.

- Refunds: C invalid. A rejected (2421, 2429, 2442, 2449). D rejected (2434, 2438, 2439). B is mixed: accepted 2440 (Omar Moreau, Client Services); rejected 2411, 2413, 2414, 2418. Avoid A/D. B worth testing, especially Client Services, but not a safe default.

- Claims: C invalid; D rejected (2422); A rejected (2430). B untested. Avoid A/C/D; try B if offered, otherwise test untested option.

- Invoices: C invalid. A rejected (2436, 2444, 2448); accepted (2432, 2435). B rejected (2425, 2426, 2441, 2445); accepted (2420, 2423, 2424). No safe default. A may still work for some Field Sales/Partner Accounts, but 2444 Field Sales A failed, so do not rely on it. B mixed.

- Shipments: C invalid. A rejected (2443, 2446, 2447); accepted (2431, 2433, 2437). B rejected (2427, 2428). A no longer preferred; recent Partner Accounts/Finance Desk A failures show no safe default. B also unreliable.

- Working rule: C always avoid. Refunds: avoid A/D; B mixed. Claims: avoid A/C/D. Invoices/shipments: A/B mixed, no safe default; use exact sender/team/request-type history only, and retest when uncertain.

Working notes — east-region ticket routing

- C (“regional office/region”) invalid in all tested cases. Never choose C.
- Routing depends on sender/team + request type + option + outcome. Track and verify per case; wording/urgency alone do not determine routing.

- Refunds: C invalid. A rejected (2421, 2429, 2442, 2449). D rejected (2434, 2438, 2439). B accepted 2440 (Omar Moreau, Client Services); rejected 2411, 2413, 2414, 2418, 2457 (Regional Ops). Avoid A/D. B only evidenced for Client Services; not a safe default.

- Claims: C invalid. A rejected (2430). D rejected (2422). B accepted 2450 (Field Sales); rejected 2456 (Partner Accounts), 2459 (Client Services). B mixed. Avoid A/C/D. Try B if offered, but verify.

- Invoices: C invalid. A rejected (2436, 2444, 2448); accepted (2432, 2435). B rejected (2425, 2426, 2441, 2445, 2455); accepted (2420, 2423, 2424). No safe default. A/B both mixed.

- Shipments: C invalid. A rejected (2443, 2446, 2447, 2451, 2452, 2453, 2454, 2458); accepted (2431, 2433, 2437). B rejected (2427, 2428). A now heavily rejected; B also unreliable. No safe default.

- Working rule: C always avoid. Refunds: avoid A/D; B only for Client Services. Claims: avoid A/C/D; B mixed. Invoices/shipments: A/B mixed, no safe default; use exact sender/team/request-type history only, and retest when uncertain.
